author: deepaks2
title: iGPU RoPE Tests fail — runner exposes only CPU, no GPU device available
signature: iGPU runner did not expose GPU (Available devices only CPU)|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: iGPU RoPE Tests / GPU_RoPE
failed_jobs.symptom: Fail-fast device gate asserts 'GPU' in Core().available_devices; only ['CPU'] was reported, so the runner's OpenCL/GPU device was not exposed to the container.

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status check fails because the GPU_RoPE job failed.

root_cause: The job_gpu_rope_tests.yml workflow includes a fail-fast pre-check (added specifically to avoid 35 cryptic per-test GPU failures) that queries Core().available_devices before running pytest and asserts 'GPU' is present. On this run, the self-hosted iGPU runner (container from image intel-gpu igpu-pr...) only exposed CPU to the OpenVINO runtime, meaning the host's Intel GPU device node (/dev/dri) was not passed through to the Docker container or the GPU driver/clinfo stack was not initialized on the runner at job start. This is a runner/host provisioning issue, not a problem with the PR's Softplus GPU kernel change — the actual RoPE pytest suite never executed because the gate assertion fired first, so no test results were produced and the follow-up artifact-upload step also failed (no HTML report file existed).
reproduction_steps: N/A — requires the specific self-hosted iGPU runner instance; cannot be reproduced without access to that host. Locally: run `python3 -c "from openvino import Core; print(Core().available_devices)"` inside the CI container/image on an iGPU-equipped host and confirm 'GPU' appears alongside 'CPU'.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed job — this is the documented, expected remedy for this fail-fast gate per the workflow's own comment ('likely infra flake, rerun the job').

If the failure recurs on the same runner, check that the runner's Docker invocation passes through --device=/dev/dri (or equivalent GPU device mapping) and that the intel-gpu drivers/OpenCL runtime are initialized before the job starts.
Consider adding a runner health-check step (e.g., clinfo) before job start that fails fast with a clearer error and triggers automatic runner recycling.
prevention_strategies: Add pre-flight GPU availability checks (clinfo / device node checks) as a separate, earlier CI step so infra flakes are caught before dependency installation, saving CI time. Track recurrence of 'runner did not expose GPU' across runs to detect a systematically unhealthy runner and trigger runner replacement.
historical_context: Other iGPU RoPE Tests failures previously recorded in the pattern DB are all Network-category (DNS/proxy resolution, HTTP/2 framing during checkout) or artifact-upload Infrastructure issues, none matching this specific 'GPU not exposed' device-gate assertion. This is a new, distinct failure signature for the iGPU RoPE Tests job.
